name: avatar-avatar-group
title: Avatar: Avatar Group
description:
Use the `AvatarGroup` component to overlap a set of avatars. Each avatar is clipped around the avatar above it, leaving a transparent gap instead of a background-colored ring.

`topmost` chooses which avatar stays whole. It defaults to `last`, which keeps a trailing `<AvatarGroupCount>` intact. Use `topmost="first"` when the first avatar should lead the stack.

Adjust the overlap with `--avatar-overlap` and the cut gap with `--avatar-gap`:

```tsx
<AvatarGroup className="[--avatar-gap:0.125rem] [--avatar-overlap:0.625rem]">
  <Avatar>...</Avatar>
  <Avatar>...</Avatar>
  <AvatarGroupCount>+3</AvatarGroupCount>
</AvatarGroup>
```

files.content:
import { Avatar, AvatarFallback, AvatarGroup, AvatarImage } from "@/registry/erbium/ui/avatar";

export default function AvatarGroupExample() {
  return (
    <AvatarGroup className="grayscale">
      <Avatar>
        <AvatarImage
          src="https://images.pexels.com/photos/1681010/pexels-photo-1681010.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=256&h=256&fit=crop"
          alt="John Doe"
        />
        <AvatarFallback>JD</AvatarFallback>
      </Avatar>
      <Avatar>
        <AvatarImage
          src="https://images.pexels.com/photos/415829/pexels-photo-415829.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=256&h=256&fit=crop"
          alt="Jane Doe"
        />
        <AvatarFallback>JD</AvatarFallback>
      </Avatar>
      <Avatar>
        <AvatarImage
          src="https://images.pexels.com/photos/2379004/pexels-photo-2379004.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=256&h=256&fit=crop"
          alt="Alex Smith"
        />
        <AvatarFallback>AS</AvatarFallback>
      </Avatar>
    </AvatarGroup>
  );
}
